I am an old woman of sixty-one years, farming this small beans plot near my compound here in the North West. The land is my family's own, so I will plant it carefully with my cowpea seeds I kept from last harvest — I cannot afford the improved seeds from the agro-dealer, and our local variety does well enough when intercropped with my millet and sorghum. I will not buy NPK for the beans because legumes fix their own nitrogen, but I will carry some of the goat and cattle manure from our compound to help the soil. My sons and daughters-in-law will help me weed, and I may hire two or three young men for one or two days when the weeds get heavy before flowering, since my back is not what it used to be.
